'''Zoltan George Hajos''' (born '''Zoltán György Hajós'''; 3 March 1926 – 9 October 2022) was a Hungarian-American [[organic chemist]]. Originally an academic in his native Budapest, then an industrial chemist in the pharmaceutical industry, he is known for the [[Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction]] (originally named Hajos-Parrish reaction by Claude Agami in 1985<ref name="Agami Levisalles Puchot 1985 pp. 441–442">{{cite journal | last1=Agami | first1=Claude | last2=Levisalles | first2=Jacques | last3=Puchot | first3=Catherine | title=A new diagnostic tool for elucidating the mechanism of enantioselective reactions. Application to the Hajos–Parrish reaction | journal=J. Chem. Soc., Chem. Commun. | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | issue=8 | year=1985 | issn=0022-4936 | doi=10.1039/c39850000441 | pages=441–442}}</ref>).

==Biography==

===Chemistry training===
<!--{{expand section|sourced information on dissertation topic, publications, fellowships, awards, etc. from graduate and post-doctoral research|small=no|date=July 2015}} -->
Hajos studied chemistry at the [[Technical University of Budapest]] (TU Budapest), in Hungary, completing an M.Sc. in 1947,<ref name="ch.bme.hu">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ch.bme.hu/document/1046/original/2013_Hajos_vd.pdf|title=Dr. Hajós Zoltán – 1926-ban született Budapesten. Vegyészmérnöki oklevelét 1947-ben szerezte, száma 465|accessdate=9 October 2021}}</ref> and his doctoral work under [[Zoltan Csuros]] of the Institute of Organic Chemical Technology in 1950.<ref name="ch.bme.hu"/>

===Early academic career===
Hajos remained there until accepting a position as [[assistant professor]] in organic chemistry at the TU Budapest in 1948, where he stayed until 1957.<ref name="dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu 2007" /><ref>[http://zooly.zl.hu/hajos/hajos_parrish.pdf Hajos-Parrish reaction mechanism]</ref> With backlash following the 1956 ''Revolution'' in October, 1956,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/soviets-put-brutal-end-to-hungarian-revolution|title=Soviets put a brutal end to Hungarian revolution|accessdate=9 October 2021}}</ref> Hajos left TU Budapest and communist Hungary for the United States, where he took a position as a research associate in organic chemistry, a senior postdoctoral-level position, in the Department of Chemistry at [[Princeton University]], beginning in 1957.<ref name="dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu 2007">{{cite web | title=Hajos, Zoltan G. Magyar Biografia | website=dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu | date=10 October 2007 | url=http://dobroka.hu/zghajos/Hajos-Zoltan-G-Magyar-Biografia.htm | language=hu | access-date=9 October 2021}}</ref>

===Second academic and pharmaceutical periods===
<!--{{expand section|sourced information on academic and pharmaceutical positions, especially if accolades such as "distinguished" are to reappear|small=no|date=July 2015}}-->
Hajos accepted a chemistry position with the Pharmaceutical Research Institute of [[Hoffmann-La Roche]], a pharmaceutical company, in [[Nutley, New Jersey]], in 1960.<ref name="dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu 2007" /> He remained in that position until beginning a second phase of an academic career in 1970, first in the Chemistry Department of the [[University of Vermont]] (1972–1973), and thereafter on the Faculty of Pharmacy of the [[University of Toronto]] (1973–1974).<ref name="dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu 2007" /> Hajos returned to the pharmaceutical industry in 1975, proceeding through a series of positions at the Research Institute of [[Johnson & Johnson]], until retiring in 1990.<ref name="dobroka.hu / dobróka.hu 2007" />

===Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction, discovery and importance===
[[File:Hajos-Parrish Patent Application 2102623.png|thumb|Front page of the German Patent Application no. 21 02 623, published July 29, 1971]]
Hajos is noted for the [[Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction]],<ref name="Kürti">László Kürti, Barbara Czakó: ''Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis''. Elsevier Academic Press, Burlington/San Diego/London 2005, {{ISBN|0-12-369483-3}}, p. 192-193.</ref> and of the related (''S'')-[[proline]]-catalyzed synthesis route to the {{ill|Hajos-Wiechert ketone|de|Hajos-Wiechert-Keton}},<ref name="Hajos-Parrish-Eder-Sauer-Wiechert Reaction p. ">{{citation | chapter=Hajos-Parrish-Eder-Sauer-Wiechert Reaction | publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc. | publication-place=Hoboken, NJ, USA | date=15 September 2010 | doi=10.1002/9780470638859.conrr290 | page=| title=Comprehensive Organic Name Reactions and Reagents | isbn=978-0-470-63885-9 }}</ref> and is considered a pioneer in the research area of [[organocatalysis]].<ref name=Clayden>Jonathan Clayden, Nick Greeves, Stuart Warren: ''Organische Chemie'', Springer Spektrum, 2013, 2. Auflage, pp.&nbsp;1240–1241. {{ISBN|978-3-642-34715-3}}.</ref>  In a recent review of the Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction as a [[name reaction]], Daniel Zerong Wang describes it, and its synonyms, thus:{{blockquote|1="This reaction was independently reported by two groups in 1971: the group of Hajos and Parrish [citing a German patent dated 29 July 1971<ref>Hajos, Z. G. and Parrish, D. R., Ger. Pat., July 29, '''1971''', DE 2102623, (priority date Jan. 21, 1970).</ref>] and the group of Eder, Sauer, and Wiechert [citing a German patent dated October 7, 1971, and a 1971 journal report in German and English translation<ref>Eder, U.; Sauer, G. and Wiechert, R., Ger. Pat., Oct 7, '''1971'''a, DE 2014757.</ref><ref name=EderSauerWeichert71b>{{cite journal | last1=Eder | first1=Ulrich | last2=Sauer | first2=Gerhard | last3=Wiechert | first3=Rudolf | title=New Type of Asymmetric Cyclization to Optically Active Steroid CD Partial Structures | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English | publisher=Wiley | volume=10 | issue=7 | year=1971b | issn=0570-0833 | doi=10.1002/anie.197104961 | pages=496–497}}</ref><ref name="Eder Sauer Wiechert 1971 pp. 492–493">{{cite journal | last1=Eder | first1=Ulrich | last2=Sauer | first2=Gerhard | last3=Wiechert | first3=Rudolf | title=Neuartige asymmetrische Cyclisierung zu optisch aktiven Steroid-CD-Teilstücken | journal=Angewandte Chemie | publisher=Wiley | volume=83 | issue=13 | year=1971a | issn=0044-8249 | doi=10.1002/ange.19710831307 | pages=492–493 | bibcode=1971AngCh..83..492E | language=de}}</ref>]. It is an enantioselective [a]ldol [r]eaction catalyzed by (''S'')-proline… [and is] one of the earliest enantioselectively catalyzed reactions of practical use in synthetic organic chemistry. Owing to its wide application in organic synthesis, it has been extensively explored and extended to asymmetric [a]ldol... α-alkylation… Mannich... Michael [a]ddition... and α-amination… [reactions] of carbonyl compounds. In the literature, this reaction has been referred to by different names: [as the Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction]... Hajos-Eder-Sauer-Wiechert... Hajos-Wiechert... and Hajos-Parrish-Wiechert reactions."<ref>Zerong Wang, 2010, "290. Hajos-Parrish-Eder-Sauer-Wiechert Reaction," in ''Comprehensive Organic Name Reactions and Reagents,'' pp. 1305–1309, New York, NY, USA:John Wiley & Sons, {{doi|10.1002/9780470638859.conrr290}}.</ref>}} Nobel Prize laureate in Chemistry 2021 [[Benjamin List]], a leader in the modern field of organocatalysis,<ref name=mpg-int>{{cite web |last=Pietschmann |first=Catarina | title=A Perspective for Life | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft | date=6 October 2021 | url=https://www.mpg.de/17662734/potrait-benjamin-list | access-date=7 October 2021}}</ref> describes the importance of the discovery of the Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction thus:{{blockquote|1="Discovered in the early 1970s, the Hajos–Parrish–Eder–Sauer–Wiechert reaction, a proline-catalyzed intramolecular aldol reaction [citing journal articles Hajos & Parrish (1974a) and Eder, Sauer & Wiechert (1971b)<ref name=EderSauerWeichert71b/><ref name=HajosParrish74a>{{cite journal | last1=Hajos | first1=Zoltan G. | last2=Parrish | first2=David R. | title=Asymmetric synthesis of bicyclic intermediates of natural product chemistry | journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=39 | issue=12 | year=1974a | issn=0022-3263 | doi=10.1021/jo00925a003 | pages=1615–1621}}</ref>], ''represents not only the first asymmetric aldol reaction invented by chemists but also the first highly enantioselective organocatalytic transformation.''<ref name="List Hoang Martin pp. 5839–5842">{{cite journal | last1=List | first1=B. | last2=Hoang | first2=L. | last3=Martin | first3=H. J. | title=Asymmetric Catalysis Special Feature Part II: New mechanistic studies on the proline-catalyzed aldol reaction | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | volume=101 | issue=16 | date=8 April 2004 | issn=0027-8424 | doi=10.1073/pnas.0307979101 | pages=5839–5842| pmid=15073330 | pmc=395996 | bibcode=2004PNAS..101.5839L | doi-access=free }}</ref>}}

==Personal life and death==
Hajos died in Budapest on 9 October 2022, at the age of 96.<ref>{{cite web |title=We are sad to inform you that Zoltan G. Hajos, a groundbreaking pioneer of #organocatalysis, has passed away. |url=https://twitter.com/soosgroup/status/1579584414635692032?lang=en-GB |website=Soos OrgCat Lab on Twitter |access-date=6 December 2022 |date=10 October 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Hajos received a Certificate of Merit, an Iron Award, from TU Budapest in May 2013, in recognition of 65 years of professional service.<ref name="ch.bme.hu" />

Hajos received a Certificate of Merit, a Ruby Award, from TU Budapest in 2017, in recognition of 70 years of professional service.<ref>{{Cite web |author-link=Budapest University of Technology and Economics |title=Arany-, Gyémánt-, Vas-, Rubin- és Platinadiplomások 2017 |url=https://www.ch.bme.hu/document/2175/original/Aranydiploma%202017%20VBK%2003[1].pdf |access-date=23 October 2022 |issn=2063-3459}}</ref>

Hajos received a Certificate of Merit, a Platinum Award, from TU Budapest in 2022, in recognition of 75 years of professional service.<ref>{{Cite web |author-link=Budapest University of Technology and Economics |title=Arany-, Gyémánt-, Vas-, Rubin- és Platinadiplomások 2022 |url=https://www.ch.bme.hu/document/2890/original/Jubileumi%20kiadv%C3%A1ny2022%20VBK.pdf |access-date=23 October 2022 |issn=2063-3459}}</ref>
